Ultimate Ears Boom 3 Portable Waterproof Bluetooth Speaker - Sunset Red I listen mostly to jazz in the background while I’m reading or on the web, usually at low volume - sometimes rock at louder volumes. I’ve bought any number of blue tooth speakers, as a hobby I suppose, always in search of that nirvana sound. They’ve ranged from really small Fugoo units (with unbelievably good sound) to paired floor standing auditorium behemoths that will blow your contacts out. IMO, the UE Boom 3’s are not only a good value, they are superlative in sound from low to high ranges at easy and medium volume. Great for voice, too, e.g. podcasts. I have 2 paired and will likely buy another pair (stereo is nice) for another room.

I recently tried the UE Megablast and they don’t hold a candle to to crispness and range of the Boom 3’s. They’re loud and have some nice control features but for sound, IMO the 3’s are the best by far, and uncannily the least expensive of over 10 other brands, up to $300. Unless you’re filling a large room with loud music I’d say the Boom is the best speaker in it’s portable class. Enjoy, and don’t worry about missing any sound - you’ll pleasantly hear it all!

text_fidelity_a:
WixGear Sport Wireless Earbuds, Bluetooth 5.0 Wireless Over Ear Sport Headphones with Touch Control, and Charging Case Stereo Deep Bass Sound,30H Playtime Sweat-Proof Bluetooth Earphones with Mic For my uses, these are great. They were very well packaged and secure for shipping. The box is very nice and sturdy, lined with foam. I need to hear the environment around me. This has been an issue with previous earbuds. Commercials between videos or songs can get so loud! That is the deal-breaker for me, as it's a safety issue. These do not get too loud, even on the loudest setting, so I am able to remain safe. I don't have an issue hearing the sounds coming from the buds, but I'm not in high-traffic outdoor areas regularly either. My ear canals are unusually small for an adult. I was afraid these may be too-big, but they are snug. Any bigger and it may have been an issue. I used the smaller of the plastic tips. Over the ear designs are the only ones that have ever worked for me. I did look at some other models in the past, but I found them a bit more expensive than I felt justified to spend unknowing how well they may work for me. However, knowing how well these work, I find them to be a really great value and would have purchased them before if I had known how well they worked. It was only by chance they were up for review and I had been seeking a replacement on my old pair that I've been using for the past few years.

The Bluetooth is nice. I have a simple cell phone. It only took asking my phone to connect to work. It was the easiest that I have ever had with connecting anything Bluetooth to my phone. I liked this as I'm not the most savvy at using Bluetooth electronics. If I can do it, anyone can.

I'm not great at using the buttons as they are really sensors on the flat-side of the body on the earbuds. I'm getting used to it but they are touch sensitive and there is a correct spot and amount of pressure that works best. I'm still getting a feel for it and there is a slight delay, so it's very easy to double-tap. The included booklet has been helpful to learn to use these straight out of the package.

Sometimes I get down on the floor at the gym to use the foam rollers and stretches, other times I'm using them in the car to take calls. I've tried them at work as well. Every scenario has worked well for me. I really do wish I've had these before. Sometimes while getting my breaks at work, I would want to listen to things from my phone, but didn't want to risk disturbing my co-workers with some of the news and hobby related videos I enjoy. I asked a few co-workers if they could hear my earbud noise, they could not.

The case is very easy to use as well and fits easily into my pockets. I'm a lady, so my pockets are not always very generously sized. It charges very quickly, and I've not found myself running out of charge. I cannot speak on the long-term durability for this as they are new. If/when I experience any issues with the charge, I will be sure to post an update.

In summary, these would be better for users that need to hear their surroundings for safety. For those that want extreme high volume, they may not be as happy. They stay on my ears securely and the case works very well. I'm pleasantly surprised how well I like these and hope that they are durable since they are working so well for me.

Thanks for reading my review. I hope you found it helpful.
text_fidelity_b: WixGear Sport Wireless Earbuds, Bluetooth 5.0 Wireless Over Ear Sport Headphones with Touch Control, and Charging Case Stereo Deep Bass Sound,30H Playtime Sweat-Proof Bluetooth Earphones with Mic

text_fidelity_a:
Bose SoundTrue Headphones Around-Ear Style, Black Bose is primarily known for their active noise canceling (ANC) phones though they have for years offered non-ANC phones. This is my first pair of Bose phones that are not in the ANC class of headphones and my impression of them is mostly positive. I do see some room for improvement, though.

First off, these are without question the lightest headphones (aside from ear buds) that I have ever worn. I am a bit odd in that I actually prefer heavier headphones but this is strictly a preference, not a criticism. In spite of the weight, the phones fit very nicely and do not feel like they're about to slip off if you lean down. This is not to say they're tight, but they are tight enough to hold well. They're easy to adjust too, so getting them to fit just right is simple enough. If exceptionally lightweight headphones are your thing, this is what you want.

The cord is a little different than other phones I have used in that the jacks on either end are of different sizes. This is good and bad. It's good in that there's no question of how to attach the cord because it only fits one way. But, it also means that a normal cord that comes with practically any other headphone will not work.

The sound quality is definitely better than average but not perfect (certainly not audiophile-level). The sound spectrum seems to be fairly well balanced. The highs are good and the "edges" are crisp and clean for most tracks. The midrange is ok but slightly hollow. The bass is very good without being overdriven. One of the problems with a lot of headphones is that they tend to overdrive the bass which is fine if you really like your bass, but too much can overpower the rest of the spectrum and give some of us headaches. That these phones do not over-amplify the bass is a pleasant surprise.

Having a pair of Bose QC-15 ANC phones, I can compare the two models' sound profiles and there are some slight differences. Where the QC-15s are great at the highs and overdrive the bass, the midrange is sorely lacking. The SoundTrue get the bass right and have good highs but fall slightly short on the midrange (though still better than the QC-15s). Comparing just the sound profiles and ignoring the ANC function, I prefer the SoundTrue over the QC-15s.

The carrying case is nice and should provide some protection when packed for travel. I would have preferred a slightly harder and more crush-resistant case but that's me being picky. There's not a lot of extra room in the case so storage is not really an option with the case.

The price is a little high ($180 as I write this) and that might be a little steep for some. It comes down to whether a less expensive set of phones delivers the same (or better) sound profile.

My overall impression of the Bose SoundTrue headphones is positive. These are very comfortable and exceptionally lightweight and the sound quality is good though not perfect. These phones are above average and are worth consideration if you want non-ANC headphones or if you're looking for very lightweight headphones.
text_fidelity_b: Bose SoundTrue Headphones Around-Ear Style, Black

FIDO2 Security Key [Folding Design] Thetis Universal Two Factor Authentication USB (Type A) for Multi-Layered Protection (HOTP) in Windows/Linux/Mac OS,Gmail,Facebook,Dropbox,SalesForce,GitHub Thus far this is the only hardware USB key that I have tried that compare to Yubbi. These are about half the price and as you should know if shopping these, you need a minimum of 2. I recommend having at least 3 to 5. If you lose, break, damage or anything causing your device to be innaccessable then in some cases, especially in Crypto exchanges you will not be able to regain access to your assets.

I keep one on me, one in a safe at my house, one in a safety deposit box and another with a trusted friend that has no idea what it goes to. These things are the best protection you can own for logging in to accounts using MFA.

This has the same compatibility as other brands. Worked everywhere it said and more. If you do anything in finance or even online banking or shopping, I would highly recommend looking into these. Not sure why Amazon hasn't added support on here for this type of MFA. Wish they would hurry up and do so. text_fidelity_a:
Soundcore Wakey Bluetooth Speaker Powered by Anker with Alarm Clock, Stereo Sound, FM Radio, White Noise, QI Wireless Charger with 7.5W Charging for iPhone and 10W for Samsung I ordered the 'Soundcore Wakey Bluetooth Speaker Powered by Anker with Alarm Clock, Stereo Sound, FM Radio, White Noise, QI Wireless Charger with 7.5W Charging for iPhone and 10W for Samsung' for review and would like to share some of my thoughts after a few weeks.

First off, this thing is actually pretty amazing. The build quality is nice and aesthetically it looks clean. The sound quality is nice but not phenomenal. However for how small it is, it does produce decent sound and for a bedside alarm clock it does quite well. The wireless charging works great for my Galaxy Note 8 (and does in fact Fast-Charge) however there have been a couple nights to where my phone was not charged the next morning. The fast charger also works with my wireless earbuds which I attached an image showing the charge light on the Wakey, and the wireless earbuds case indicating charging. However for the wireless earbud charging, it does take some precise positioning to get them to charge. I noticed in other review that others weren't happy with the bright display light with no way to adjust it any dimmer than the lowest setting, however they must have updated that with a firmware update (which was super easy to do) as I had no issues with the display being too bright at night. I use the auto adjust setting which seems to work quite well as far as I can tell. Also I love the sleep mode sounds that you can adjust several (or just one) sound volumes to create your own personalized preference. I do wish that there were more sound options but the ones they provide are acceptable. I also wish that you could download and install more alarm sounds. Bluetooth connectivity is super quick and have never once had an issue with pairing it up to my phone. Really the ONLY issue I have with the Wakey is that to get the sleep mode sounds going, you need to connect with the app, and via Bluetooth connect to the device. No big deal right? Well my concern is that you will need to keep it connected for this feature to work. This means you will be connected to the Wakey ALL night and this kind of bugs me. It's just kind of creepy that the Wakey is connected to your phone all night while you sleep. I wish there was a way to just play your favorite white noise sleep sound by pressing a button on the Wakey device without having to always connect and stay connected to the app and your phone. The other gripe is that the plug design is huge and makes it so that I have had to move my nightstand further way from the wall to use it. Other than those two gripes, and the only reason for docking one star, the Soundcore Wakey is a very good product and a really great value.
*On a side note - I just tested the Wakey while watching some Youtube videos and the latency is not so good. There is quite a bit of delay and the voices do not sync up at all so I wouldn't recommend using the Wakey for listening to videos.
text_fidelity_b: Soundcore Wakey Bluetooth Speaker Powered by Anker with Alarm Clock, Stereo Sound, FM Radio, White Noise, QI Wireless Charger with 7.5W Charging for iPhone and 10W for Samsung

text_fidelity_a:
Kensington Wired SlimBlade Trackball Mouse (K72327U), Black I lived and breathed full-sized Kensington trackball mice from about 1987 until my last one stopped functioning and I couldn't find them anymore...probably in the late '90s. Tried some others; all had small, lightweight balls that gave none of the feel and control of Kensinton's...Expert Mouse? Was that what it was called back then too? Because it was the same general design as the current Expert Mouse, but the body was computer-case white.

Anyway, I had several of those (the quality going downhill with each iteration, as I recall) and loved them, and since they disappeared (as far as I could tell), I adapted, first to trackpads, which I've never liked much, and then back to traditional mice which don't give nearly the control of a trackball. Now, at last, it seems Kensington has again begun to produce truly worthwhile trackball mice, and this is one. Oh, it's _so_ good to have one of these again.

I'm doing that thing I hate when other people do it and reviewing the product as soon as I've gotten it up and running, without any kind of experiential history behind my assessment. I'll come back and update this in the future if necessary. But so far: I'm happy, happy, happy to have a real, full-sized Kensington trackball mouse again, with a heavy, substantial ball. There are only two things about this device that I'm not crazy about: In my old Kensington mice, the ball rested on physical rollers and I could give the ball a good spin and it would keep spinning for a second before stopping; it spun much more freely in its cavity than this ball does (so far...maybe that's something that will break in?) [Update: yes, after about three days of use the ball rolls more smoothly and silently than the old one on rollers ever did]. And the other thing is the scrolling mechanism. It's weird. Despite the KensingtonWorks software trying to make us believe otherwise, the "scroll ring" itself actually has nothing to do with scrolling, nor with anything else - the "scroll ring" is not even a control, but just a static piece of chrome trim. What makes the mouse scroll is twisting the ball this way or that from the top, as if it were a knob. At first I thought the "scroll ring" wasn't working because I was trying to use it without touching the ball...which does nothing. And now that I've figured out how scrolling works (you rest your finger on the "scroll ring" and push and pull the side of the ball)...I'm not crazy about it. I'm getting used to it, but it's just a weird way to scroll (I can't for the life of me remember how I used to do it on the Expert Mouse decades ago). It does work though.

(Update on the scrolling: I'm also not crazy about the way the KensingtonWorks software handles the scrolling speed adjustment. When you make the base pointer movement speed faster, the pointer continues to move smoothly, but just faster. When you make the scrolling speed faster though, you lose all smoothness - the software makes the scrolling faster by breaking it into successively larger and more jarring jumps. At the slowest speed, it's pretty smooth; at the highest speeds it's no longer really scrolling, but simply jumping abruptly from one screenful (or page) to the next. Increasing the scrolling speed just increases the size of these jumps, but I find them jarring and annoying starting at the second or third lowest speed setting.)

I also had to figure out how to program one of the buttons as a click lock, since Kensington doesn't call it that anymore, but calls it "left drag", "right drag", and "middle drag" (and I have no idea what the difference is between those three - I just chose "left drag" and it's working fine).

So far, those are my only gripes, all minor. So happy to have one of these things again! =) (Did I mention that?)

Enjoy...
text_fidelity_b: Kensington Wired SlimBlade Trackball Mouse (K72327U), Black

text_fidelity_a: DB Link RT4 4-Gauge Ring Terminal (2 Red and 2 Black) I received this order in a short time from placing the order.  The gold plated lugs are a good finish to make them look goldish, can't say if it is or not.  The inside diameter is 0.41 inch or 10.42mm.  The outside diameter of the Ring Terminal is 0.703in or 17.86mm.  The inside diameter of the cable lug hole is 0.331in. or 8.4mm and I noticed it does have a significant burr on the inside of the hole, thus reducing the inside diameter somewhat.  This burr when crimping will keep wire from being placed in the hole and bite the copper some during the crimp, abrading the wire. The slip-on insulation is easy to slide on and off the terminal so the cable should be easy to install. These terminals are good enough to make a proper cable end and I give them a four star rating for quality and pricing.
text_fidelity_b: DB Link RT4 4-Gauge Ring Terminal (2 Red and 2 Black)

APC External Battery Pack, BR24BPG, Supplemental Battery for UPS Model BR1500G (Sold Separately) One of the main reasons I selected this model is the simplicity of a single battery cartridge design. My previous APC UPS units use spade connectors. I have limited use of my hands and fingers which makes it a challenge to use spade connectors so I was looking forward to the cartridge battery simplicity. When the product arrived I installed it as per the clear and easy to follow directions. But the UPS acted as if the battery was not connected and / or missing altogether. After spending a considerable time diagnosing the problem I finally removed the cartridge battery (Aaa-gain) to make a close inspection. I found there are two male blade connectors located within a pocket in the cartridge battery. Two female blade connectors are located in a protrusion inside the UPS unit battery compartment so as to self align and engage the male blades inside the pocket in the cartridge battery when the cartridge battery is installed and seated fully. One of the two male blade connectors is either missing or pressed in too deep to be reached by the mating coupling. I made a feeble attempt to tug at the stubby male blade sunk deep within the socket but gave up when I realized how stupid the situation is. This is a brand new product so why should I attempt to make a risky repair?

The problem as I see it is in attempting to get two flimsy electrical connectors to self align the first time every time all the time. If they had used common banana jacks instead of spade connectors it would only cost a penny more yet be so much more reliable.

As I write this I am awaiting a reply from APC. If APC will not take care of this problem then I will return my purchase to Amazon.com for a refund. I will follow up with the remedy after it is complete.
text_fidelity_b: APC External Battery Pack, BR24BPG, Supplemental Battery for UPS Model BR1500G (Sold Separately)

Mom and dad love them too, so we can’t really fault the two pre- teens from using and enjoying their electronics to the fullest. We like it best when they are at least devoting some of their electronic time to doing things more constructive and/or creative, and this is what convinced me to get my hands on this SOSUN Camcorder.

I had not heard of SOSUN until I got this camcorder, but I had read good things about the brand and decided that such a large percentage of customers must be right about something. One of my girls wanted a camcorder and this one seemed to have what she needed and seemed good for a beginner. The camera is lightweight and easy to hold. It can be used for regular picture taking and for video. The quality of video produced is good, too. There are better camcorders out there that create better videos and have more features, but this one is still good for a beginner like my 13 year old.

The battery life on this camcorder is about 2 hours. Given my kid’s short attention span, this is more than enough to keep her happy. In fact, she typically creates videos that are only two to five minutes in length. Unless her habits change, the 2 hour battery life is more than sufficient.

Camcorders can get expensive , especially if your needs and demands are high. But if you’re looking for a good starter camcorder for a very low price, this SOSUN is going to be difficult to match. The low price and above average quality make it worth the purchase and my increasingly more creative middle school age kid can vouch for its worthiness.

text_fidelity_a:
iHome iAVS16 Bedside Speaker with Alexa Built In, Bluetooth, and USB Charging, Now Supports Spotify by Voice This is a pretty mixed review of an interesting concept that is pretty good right now, but has the potential to be great in the near future. At the current price of about $150, this is ok+ based on the following criteria:

Sound Quality: 2.5-3 stars
For the size, it's ok
When reviewing for sound quality, I compare speakers (and headphones) to comparably sized items, based on speakers I currently or previously have owned. I take price range *somewhat* into account (I don't expect $15 headphones to sound like $500 ones), but for anything over $100, I use the full range from the cheapest stuff I have, to my favorite brand, Bose.
So with that in mind, I have a portable wireless Bose speaker that is smaller and acts as the "5" on the scale.
The sound on this can get loud enough to not distort and still fill a smallish room or normal bedroom fine. The treble and bass are ok, though the higher ranges are tinny and the bass lacks depth. Overall sound from high to low and throughout the mid range lack definition. It's good enough for very casual background listening and for podcasts.

Alexa Feature: 4 stars
I have an iPhone and think Alexa has quite a bit more understanding and skill than Siri. When asked questions, from simple stuff like "what's the weather" to more complicated stuff like "I'm hungry. What can I make in half an hour?", the answers and follow-up questions are highly intuitive and thorough. Does she get everything all the time? No. But she does a much better job than Siri.

User-Friendliness: 2.5 stars
I didn't like the process of figuring out how this works, particularly the part of pairing with more than one device and also Having to use an app to make most of it work. It was a clunky, irritating process that more or less stayed that way every time I wanted to use this thing, especially for listening to music. It should be able to just play from your iTunes through the iTunes app and bluetooth, and instead, I was only able to make it play iTunes though Their App, which sucks when it comes to my music. And that brings us to the App..

App: 2 stars
No. Just no. Bluetooth exists for a reason, and if a speaker has bluetooth, you should be able to just pair and play. I had to use the app to play from my iTunes, and because I have a very specific way of organizing things, I was incredibly annoyed that something didn't translate, and my music was disorganized and basically impossible to search for with this app. Instead of being able to play what I want from one of my playlist subfolders, it disregarded my way of organizing things, and I ended up giving up. If I can't listen to my stuff easily with this, then like 75% of the reason to use this disappears, leaving me with an expensive alarm clock with weather report, recipe ideas, and some cool internet stuff. That's cool, but it's quite incomplete for what I need, and what I suspect many people want.

tl;dr version: sound is mediocre but doable, app is bad, Alexa is super clever and smart, and the experience has a lot of frustrating aspects.
text_fidelity_b: iHome iAVS16 Bedside Speaker with Alexa Built In, Bluetooth, and USB Charging, Now Supports Spotify by Voice

text_fidelity_a:
Microsoft Wireless Comfort Desktop 5000 Not being a techie, this review will be based on the experiences of an average Joe or Jane trying this keyboard on for size.

Pros:

1. Excellent packaging. Easy to open, and is packed in a compact and attractive box. Would make a great gift.
2. Nice comfortable palm rest and key positioning. The removable feet required a bit of reading of the instructions to set up, but this was relatively easily accomplished. Note: Be careful you don't throw out the feet with the packaging.
3. Easy set up. Up and running in minutes.
4. Works with batteries, so no need to store and locate a charger when the mouse runs out of steam. (As compared to the Logitech model)
5. Handy buttons for MS Office, such as cut, copy, paste, undo, bold, italic and underline (et al) right on the keyboard. (as dual key functions)
6. Media keys and volume controls on keyboard, also low battery indicator light.
7. Compact footprint, so it can fit most workstations.

Cons:

1. Can you say "dust magnet"? This thing picks up dust and fingerprints like crazy, especially on the shiny bits.
2. Lack of detailed instructions for the keyboard and mouse. It comes with adequate set-up instructions, but expects you to know what to do after that. I'd have appreciated some included info on the keyboard functions.
3. No lights for Caps lock and Num lock
4. Mouse has no on/off switch (that I can find), so when I turned it over and put in the batteries (2 x AA included) I nearly blinded myself with the blue laser. Note: It turns off when the receiver is stored in the base.
5. Mouse is obese. Hard for small hands to deal with, and not ergonomic.

Note:
I don't have Windows 7 as yet, but it's nice to know that whenever I get it, the keyboard has special "hot keys" to allow easy access to programmes.

Overall, a good keyboard/mouse combination for the price, with more positive features than negative if you're an average computer user. I can't speak for Gamers or Techies, but I like it.

Amanda Richards, January 3, 2010
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Wireless Comfort Desktop 5000

text_fidelity_a:
Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) I received a Kindle as a gift, and it has taken over my reading life. I'm sad when a book is only available in print and delighted when there is a Kindle version. It's not AS comfortable as a print book, it's MORE comfortable than a print book. The font is amazing. It's easy to use, and for people who knit, it sits nicely in a bookstand on or a reader's pillow to read while knitting.

I have the Sony eReader. I used to own the rocket. I see the Kindle as the real future of ebooks, and I really want ebooks to succeed for a few reasons.

One is storage. If you are a bibliophile, you probably have a book army ready to take over your home. We avid readers are forced to cull our libraries to make room for new books. No more. I would suggest opening a free account with a service like Goodreads to categorize books, since with the Kindle you can't set up a "history" section and a "fantasy" section, but that's so minor. I never could keep those organized in my print library as well, and many books fall into multiple categories anyway. Do I need to mention that ebooks don't yellow and decay over time?

Two is portability. If you are the type to carry many books at once (I am--some for study and some for pleasure reading along with a newspaper) then this is the easiest way to do it.

Three is the glorious possibility that books will never go "out of print" again, because there is no "print" overhead, just a little meg sitting in a several terrabyte raid array somewhere. Books will always be a minute away.

Four is the idea that books will be instantly large print and still small, and easy to tote around. My eyes are still quite good, but I'd love to think, when age degrades them someday, I'll still be able to read the latest releases easily.

Five is the instant availability of hot books. When Brisingr came out, it was sitting on my Kindle that morning. Compare that to the sometimes day-long wait we went through for the Harry Potter books (and books that size are yet another reason ebooks rock). I love having the New York Times delivered, but can't stand it when the delivery boy loses the key and rings my bell at 4 in the morning. This is the best of both worlds.

Six is the ease of reading large online documents, such as those from Gutenberg or a friend's novel (and don't we all have someone who sends us large files to read from time to time?)

Seven is the price of the books. Everything is cheaper on the Kindle and some books are frighteningly inexpensive. I bought the Talmud for 99 cents. A collection of the first five books in the John Carter on Mars series for 99 cents. And the entire collection of the Wizard of Oz books for, you guessed it, 99 cents.

Other e-readers hit close to the mark; the Kindle got it right. I only want two things. I want color and I want Amazon to hit that goal of having every book (including comics and manga please) available for the Kindle. Overall, the day of the ebook truly arrived with the Kindle and I couldn't be happier.
text_fidelity_b: Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th)

text_fidelity_a:
Vizio VAP430 Co-Star Streming Media Client (Black) I really want to like the Co-Star, but it's just not there yet.

Pros
* Simple - Easy to set up and use.
* Remote - Other than the delay mentioned in cons, the remote performs beautifully.
* UI - Vizio did a great job altering the stock Google TV UI.

Cons
* Connectivity - The device doesn't seem to want to stay connected to my WiFi. It also doesn't always auto-reconnect when it loses the signal. It's worked great ever since I started using a Cat5 cable instead.
* Apps - The App store is filled with mostly terrible apps at the moment. I was excited about the Amazon app, but it literally just launches the Amazon webpage. Really Amazon!?!?!
* Blocked content - This isn't an issue with the device, as much as content providers' reaction to it. Major content sites like Comedy Central and Hulu have blocked Google-TV. This can be fixed by altering the user-agent in advanced Chrome settings, but 1) that leads to a desktop site that's harder to navigate and 2) most people won't know to do that.
* Flash player - Again, this isn't necessarily an issue with the device, but Flash tends to crash or run very slowly on it.
* Delayed input - The remote seems to have a 0-1 second processing delay (normally closer to 0), but this leads to you double pressing buttons and ending up in the wrong place.

I would rate the experience much lower than my media center PC and about on par with Roku II (which I also think is flawed).
text_fidelity_b: Vizio VAP430 Co-Star Streming Media Client (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Pivotal Living Tracker 1 (2nd Generation) Black (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I came to this tracker cold. The Housemate has a Fitbit, but I never used it, and really haven't paid a lot of attention to what it did so I had no expectations of what the Pivotal Living tracker might do. However before I tell you what I discovered, let me explain some things about myself. I'm in my sixties, and have a sedentary job. I would like to be more active, I would like to compare my actual sleep habits against what I perceive them to be, I would like to keep an eye on hydration. I have some other goals, but these are the main ones that apply to my use of the tracker.

So how does the Pivotal Living tracker stand up to these goals? First off, because so much of my everyday movement is not easily measurable by the tracker, I'm not really getting an accurate step count. (Moving around the house holding things doesn't always register. Sitting and doing something like folding laundry sometimes does.) This is a bit of a problem because it makes it difficult to estimate how I'm doing on my step goal. So, accuracy in step count? Not so much. Going to stick to a pedometer or pedometer app. C, maybe C+ because I can set my own goals based on my health and how my day is going. (Right now I have a torn meniscus, and all my steps are limping or cane-assisted. Not fun, and not conducive to accurate step counts.)

Hydration? Great, unless you forget to enter an amount until after midnight. Whoops, sorry, can't add anything to your daily total. This is a huge oversight IMO. I sometimes finish my daily amount late in the evening when I'm not thinking about using the mobile app. However, the process of tracking it on your own is a good one. They simply need to fix the access problem. B+

Daily activity. Honestly I have NO clue how this is tracked. I'd have thought it was step-based, but I've never yet had daily activity show up on my dashboard, so there has to be some other way this band tracks activity. However, having an activity alarm that reminds me to stop what I'm doing, get up and walk around for a few minutes... that's immensely valuable to me. Without it, I'd simply forget and keep on writing or editing. I'm going to give it an A because I love the alarm which can be set for 20/40/or 60 minutes.

The rest? Sleep alarm... I've been wakened by this exactly once, when I was very nearly awake anyway. Every other morning it's done zip. I'll wake up an hour later and think, "Wha?" It's back to my clock radio. C, at best. However the sleep tracker seems surprisingly accurate based on what I remember of my nights. It fairly accurately charts how many times I've woken up, and how much good sleep I've gotten. I find this quite reassuring. A, even A+.

Calories burned: Since this is both step and activity based, it's pretty useless for me. Anyway, my goal isn't about calories, it's about activity, so I'm not going to grade this part of the app. Also, weight: Clearly this is another sub-app like hydration, which requires you to input your numbers. It keeps my weight in front of me which is a good thing, but it's not really something I feel I can adequately grade.

Problem: If you take it off it will turn itself off. I tried to put it on my desk when I was typing since it interfered with the position of my wrist. I could hear the activity alert when the band buzzed against the desk, but then it stopped because the tracker had shut down. I thought it was out of juice and couldn't figure out why I was getting less than 24 hours on the battery. When I finally figured it out, I had to start wearing it up high on my arm. Fortunately the band is big enough to allow it to sit several inches above my wrist.

Price: Very, very good. I recognize that the modest cost of the tracker is intended to get you to buy the yearly subscription, but I don't mind that. If the service works, I'm happy to pay $1 a month for it. That's still minor league stuff. However I get frequent errors saying that the goal information can't be updated from the site, and I get odd readings on my dashboard. However, by the end of the day it's usually sorted itself out, so I don't have a lot of quibbles so far.

Overall, and taking price into account I think I'd give this a B, at least for my needs. It reminds me of the things I need to remember to do, and it gives me a place where I can keep track of those goals. The cost to do this is, as I indicated, quite modest. If you're not ready to drop a lot of money on a more sophisticated tracker, give the Pivotal Living tracker a try.

Note: I'm using this on a Fire phone, which means I had to side-load the app. The instructions on how to install Google Play and everything else you need to side load Google Play apps are available on You Tube, and it's dead easy. Once you've done that, just go to the Play Store and download the Pivotal Living app, and have at it.
text_fidelity_b: Pivotal Living Tracker 1 (2nd Generation) Black (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Sony X90J 50 Inch TV: BRAVIA XR Full Array LED 4K Ultra HD Smart Google TV with Dolby Vision HDR and Alexa Compatibility XR50X90J- 2021 Model , Black After almost 3 weeks with this television, I am amazed and very, very happy with it. There's a lot to like here and a couple of things that I wasn't expecting from any television.

First is the ease of set up. Our previous smart tv was a ROKU and reasonably simple to set up as well. The Google connection here means just signing in with your existing Google info and the tv uploads your existing apps. Just like moving to your new Android phone or tablet. All of our streaming apps populated and we were able to sign in without drama - HBOMAX, Prime, Paramount Plus, HULU and Netflix. We only stream and haven't used cable or satellite in 5 years, so easy app access with a new tv is important.

The 4K picture is outstanding. There's no distortion in picture quality or digital noise even from old 1940s movies. The colors are rich and full and the tv settings let you adjust to your preference as well. We've watched a lot, A LOT of tv recently and every show on all platforms has been gorgeous. Frankly, we probably watch way too much tv as a rule and that's not going to change. I've been amazed at the picture quality difference between our year old HD tv and this one.

We've connected Alexa to this tv and the voice controls work...most of the time. Using the voice control via the remote control renders better responses for sure. The tv has recognized a Fire stick, Roku Express stick, and a portable DVD player for us without any drama. We don't have a gaming system, though.... I'm considering buying one for this giant screen.

But my final show stopper moment with this television has been the sound quality. We've never had a tv that didn't require a sound bar. Until now. Despite the tv being quite thin and lightweight, the speakers still produce a deep sound quality without any tinny undertones. The settings have a calibration option for the speakers that you definitely need to do for the best sound - it works. I truly believe this is the best television we've ever owned.

Jabra VOX Corded Stereo Headphones I confess, I'm not one for listening to things on earphones. I'm not attached to my iPod (I don't even have one). I don't listen to music on the bus or during lunch or anything like that. I have music on my smartphone, but I usually either plug it into the radio in my car via a cassette adapter and listen to it over the car speakers, or plug it into a speaker we got as a Christmas gift that is for use on music players/smartphones. So I all I had was a coupla dollar set of earphones from Micro Center when I absolutely had to use earphones. They were cheap and comfortable. Really, how much better can a high-priced couple of wires and earpieces be?

With my old earphones I could hear the fan and the television running in the background, and the sound was a bit smothered. When I changed to the Jabra VOX earphones I was awed. The sound was excellent! The "smothered" sound was non-existent and the bass was especially good (I was listening to a podcast and the host has a nice deep voice). When I switched to music, the sound was much richer and I could hear a wider range of sound, and, again, the bass was excellent.

Plus the earphones come with a free app you can download that organizes your music. You can set playlists, view album covers, and it even has an equalizer.

If good sound is your goal while listening to your music device/smartphone, this is an excellent choice. My old blue earphones are going into the emergency bin as of now!

I didn't have any problems during the activation of my device: I thought that the steps were explained clearly by the Customer Service representative, who talked with me clearly and politely during our approximately 20-minute telephone call.

I have not yet retired and like the fact that this device can travel with me to work and back.

The only problem that I encountered was that initially I could not get the device to turn off. Consequently, I really couldn't figure-out whether or not it was "on" because I didn't know how to tell the difference between off and on. After several days, the "off/on" button worked properly, and I've learned that a voice speaks when it powers off and on in a way that is similar to the procedure that a cell phone uses when it powers on and off.

Because of the problem above, the cell phone was actually "on" for several days. I didn't recharge it during that time. The unit has a small "ready" light that blinks to show that the device is operating properly. The device continued blinking all week, and I am re-charging the device now and hoping to restore the full battery charge, indicated by a steady green light on the battery indicator.

It couldn't be simpler. I understand that a cell phone can be used to call 911, as well; however, it takes awhile for my cell phone to power up. It's not always easy to use. This device is simple and, hopefully, works as well as promised.

I am pleased with the battery life and so far am pleased with everything. Hope it isn't needed but am glad to have it.
text_fidelity_b: GreatCall 5Star Urgent Response Medical Alert Device (Silver)

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin 010-02172-31 Vivoactive 4S, Smaller-Sized GPS Smartwatch, Features Music, Body Energy Monitoring, Animated Workouts, Pulse Ox Sensors and More, Light Gold with Light Pink Band I have owned this watch for a year and a half now. I use it almost daily for my walks/runs, weight workouts, and indoor bike workouts. The main reason I chose this watch in the first place was because it was one of the smaller ones available. I am 5'9 but have small wrists, and really disliked the 'utilitarian' look of larger watches. After a year and a half, I am so tired of the issues with it and ready to jump ship. If I used this watch more regularly (I only wear it for workouts - not all day), I would have switched a LONG time ago. The amount of people who have complained about the same issues for YEARS without Garmin doing anything makes me hesitant to purchase another Garmin product, especially with the Apple Watch, Samsung, and now Google buying out Fitbit and coming up with a watch.
- Spotify on this watch seriously sucks. If you check Spotify forums, you will find COUNTLESS threads of suggestions for the Spotify app on this watch that should truly be basic features at this price. Do they implement them or listen? No. Also, there is no way to contact Spotify customer service - you just get pointed towards their 'community forum' where you have people complaining of the same exact things with no fix. You can't skip forward on any track, at all. I listen to a lot of podcasts when I walk. Some are 2 hours in length while my walk is only 1 hour. This watch constantly either reverts to the very beginning of my podcast so I have to start all over (because again, you can't skip forward - so have fun listening to ads as well!) in anything, only updates 1 song out of 15 on my playlist or get the error 'sync failed', or some other random issue. Also, if you have a playlist on Spotify, you cannot choose the track you want to listen to. You have to hit the >> button to get to where you want. Really? I hope Garmin drops Spotify because they have been a truly horrible app on this watch the entire time with no effort to make updates. Take a look at the reviews of Spotify on the Garmin store if you don't believe me.
- Battery life is a couple of days. However, there are points in time where my watch will be at say 80% the night before, I get ready to leave and go my walk the next morning, pick up my watch, and it's at 8%. WTF? This happens enough to be super annoying and apparently is not an 'only me' problem. It appears to be tied to when the watch updates.
- I tried to wear this to track my sleep in the beginning and gave up after two nights due to the extreme disco effect of the 'gesture' motions. I tried turning on the 'do not disturb' function advertised on the watch which is supposed to disable this stupidly bright light that WILL wake you and whoever is next to you up. Didn't work. Do a search for 'Garmin watch lights up in middle of the night' and you will find all sorts of people complaining of the same thing, and not just on this version of the watch.
- GPS has issues connecting and can take several minutes which is pretty annoying when you try to start tracking an activity only to see a red bar when trying to connect. I 'sync' my watch to my phone constantly so that is not the issue. I have switched between the GPS options Garmin offers on the watch to no avail. Search for this issue as well and you will see lots of people with the same complaint.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin 010-02172-31 Vivoactive 4S, Smaller-Sized GPS Smartwatch, Features Music, Body Energy Monitoring, Animated Workouts, Pulse Ox Sensors and More, Light Gold with Light Pink Band

text_fidelity_a:
Western Digital 3TB WD Purple Surveillance Internal Hard Drive HDD - SATA 6 Gb/s, 64 MB Cache, 3.5" - WD30PURZ I purchased this as a data storage/backup drive for my desktop PC. My main drive is a1TB NVME drive. The data drive I use for movies, songs, and backups and digital images. Since I am not booting with the drive I don't care about raw performance, nor will I pay for it. With that said I am VERY happy with this drive. It only spins at 5400 RPM, so the access time is slightly slower, but it makes no difference to me. Maximum transfer rate is nearly 200MB/sec. High capacity drives have dense platters and are able to pull data faster.

I am a Nazi for eliminating extraneous sound and used to keep my drives inside enclosures to reduce sound. My quietest drive to date is the Samsung HD 503HI, and this is even quieter. I have several large case fans spinning slowly and if I turn them off I can ever so slightly hear a faint humming or click, but otherwise I hear NOTHING.

This is my first WD drive (have always used Samsung). I cannot speak to the drive's reliability as I've only had it for one month. It is labeled for "Surveillance," so if it's meant to be running 24/7- 365 it is meant to get use in commercial/industrial environments.

I think everyone with a desktop PC should adopt this system. It is very easy to backup anything important- save it to your C: drive as well as your backup E: drive or whatever. If one your main drive goes kaput you have the backup to pull your saved data from. You can use flash drives for additional redundancy and portability, but in my experience they are not so reliable.
text_fidelity_b: Western Digital 3TB WD Purple Surveillance Internal Hard Drive HDD - SATA 6 Gb/s, 64 MB Cache, 3.5" - WD30PURZ

NETGEAR DOCSIS 3.0 - High Speed Cable Modem (CMD31T) I have nothing but high praise for this Netgear CMD31T Cable Modem. The instructions were clear and no-nonsense; the physical installation took less than two minutes.

I would however, like to give NEGATIVE 5 stars to Comcast's ridiculous telephone service. I called the toll-free number that is provided on my bill and with the modem's paperwork. After wading through endless automated prompts, I was told that my waiting time would be 39-50 minutes. I sat and waited... After about 15 minutes, my call was disconnected. I went through the same ordeal again. After a total of close to an hour, I finally got to talk to someone - just to be told that they couldn't help me there; I needed to call a different number.

I called the new number. When I finally talked to someone there, she told me that she couldn't help me; I needed to call a different number. She read the "different" number to me - yes, the same number that I just called her on! I finally talked her into transferring me.

The person that I was transferred to didn't speak English very well. After repeating the Serial Number and the Mac ID many, many times to him, he finally got it. But it ends up that he couldn't actually help me either - he said that he would put me on hold to contact the correct person to do the switch over. When he put me on hold, he disconnected me...

I called again. 'Got someone else that barely spoke English. He said that my new modem was now in their system and that he would send a test signal. The signal did not make it to my modem for some reason. He asked me to unplug the modem from the power strip that it's on and plug it directly into the wall. I told him that I wasn't going to do that; it was obviously getting power. He then asked me to hold, so he could transfer me to tech support. When he put me on hold, I was disconnected again.

I decided that if the modem was showing up in their system now, maybe I could getting it working myself. I unplugged and replugged the power, and waited about 10 minutes. Then I unplugged and replugged my router's power. Success! It's working fine now.

Outdoor WiFi Security Camera, HD 1080P Wireless Survenience IP Camera with 32GB SD Card, IP66 Waterproof Bullet Camera for Home, Support Motion Detection FTP 65ft Night Vision Remote View Onvif Cam I selected this camera to mount on my front porch, with the intention of keeping a watchful eye on the front of the house. I was very skeptical of this camera because of the price and assumed that it would be a budget-grade solution as a result. It has proven to be better than I anticipated.

This is a single-camera solution with no dedicated monitoring station. It connects via the WiFi network and it can be monitored via phone which is handy when you’re away. It includes a power supply and all of the mounting equipment (minus the tools) to set it all up for outdoor use.

All of that sounds great, but as I write this the camera sells for under $40.

It has not performed like a $40 camera. It has been rock-solid so far – it’s stable, it has remained connected except for when I have had router issues, the image in the daytime is excellent and the night-vision mode is far and away better than I expected – I can read license plates on cars in the driveway at night.

This is not a complete security solution but rather is a single camera for zone security. There are more complete systems that offer more features and capabilities, but these cost a lot more and cover broader areas with multiple cameras. If you just need a single camera to monitor a fairly small area, and you have a wireless network to connect it to, this is a very affordable solution.
text_fidelity_b: Outdoor WiFi Security Camera, HD 1080P Wireless Survenience IP Camera with 32GB SD Card, IP66 Waterproof Bullet Camera for Home, Support Motion Detection FTP 65ft Night Vision Remote View Onvif Cam

TomTom Via 1525SE 5 Inch GPS Navigation Device with Free Traffic, Free Maps of the US, Advanced Lane Guidance and Spoken Turn-By-Turn Directions This GPS is a real upgrade for me, but I still love my old one which is TomTom One. Too bad it's no longer supported by TomTom or I probably would not have chosen the TomTom Via 1525 to try out for review. The very first thing I noticed about it was that the screen was twice as large as on my One - a very coveted perk to me. I choose to still use separate GPS devices instead of my phone since my phone uses up data and the GPS doesn't, saving me $$.

I have only used the Via 1525 a couple of times and it worked perfectly. I had to make a new account to TomTom to update it and overall it took about an hour and a half. I had a couple of problems with the update and had to restart but it finally worked. It comes with a USB for charging from a computer and another to use in the auxiliary power port in the car, and a mounting disk to adhere to a good spot in the car. It's not as intuitive as I would like, but it's not hard to figure out and it took us straight to our destination both times. I purposely passed some streets it was telling to me turn on to just to see how fast it would recalculate a route and it recalculated quickly. It has a lot of options that are indicated on the product page, most of which I will probably not use.

It's too early yet to give it 5 stars, but definitely 4 for now. It's a GPS, it found satellites quickly, got me a route planned out and was easy to follow. What more do I want from it? I like it a lot. It's supposed to have lifetime traffic and lifetime maps.......or until TomTom stops supporting it too.

IFOOTAGE On-Camera Video Light, RGB Led light for Photography, APP Control/Keyframes, CRI 95+/2700-10000K, 2000mAh/Type C Charging, Mobile Video Cconference Light, Multiple Mounting Methods, C4/Yellow I'm impressed. This little guy is strong and bright! I've tried several lights, including handheld (like this), panel lights, ring lights, etc., and I have been very impressed with this one.

Before I dive into the good, let me discuss the bad: the iPhone app. I'm all for having an app to control the light and I totally understand why it's necessary. HOWEVER, this app REQUIRES that you sign up with an email and password. While there might be benefits to this (like accessing presets/settings across devices); I didn't check. Registering an account should 100% be optional. There is no reason to require me to register with my email + password so I can control this light via Bluetooth. As an aside, according to the Apple App Store, the developer does not collect any data from your phone (see pic); this is the reason I did not deduct a star for this.

My second gripe with the app, is that the it is a little rudimentary. Not particularly polished; and a little buggy at times (e.g. I couldn't get effects to kick in after selecting them on the app (I'd have to do it multiple times before the light would react), the light wouldn't always connect on the first try, etc. This was not the norm, but it happened a few times during my testing.

Now onto the good: First and foremost, it is BRIGHT. Brighter than similarly-sized lights. Physically, it feels well-designed. It has a 2000 mAh battery (I expected 1000 mAh). It is intuitive to operate and you can use it without the app if necessary (setting color temp, intensity, etc. No effects). There is a USB-C port for charging and a small display on the top, which shows battery %, time remaining (!), and color settings.

The soft cover on the front is attached magnetically, and can be attached to the back when you take it off (!); a wonderful design touch that is much appreciated. The light can also be affixed to metal surfaces via the magnet in the back.

The app, while barebones, provides a lot of functionality. There are many effects to choose from, and even a "music" mode in which the light will pulse to the beat of music picked up by your iPhone (or whatever device you are running the app on).

Overall, I have been really pleased with this light.
text_fidelity_b: IFOOTAGE On-Camera Video Light, RGB Led light for Photography, APP Control/Keyframes, CRI 95+/2700-10000K, 2000mAh/Type C Charging, Mobile Video Cconference Light, Multiple Mounting Methods, C4/Yellow

text_fidelity_a:
Philips SHE9850 in-Ear Headphones with Advanced Acoustics (Discontinued by Manufacturer) Some people prefer their headphones outside of their ears, with comfortable ear cushions and other features, such as the [[ASIN:B00007056H Koss KTXPRO1 Titanium Portable Headphones with Volume Control]]. Others prefer wearing their headphones in the privacy of their own ears, with the added bonus of noise isolation.

There are good reasons for choosing either type depending on your personal preferences, such as comfort levels, where and when you're using them, what you're listening to, and whether or not you have to share with other people.

For general use at home, I use the regular "outie", especially for movies or music with inappropriate language that I'd rather not play in surround sound in the presence of young `uns. I also let my son use it when I'd rather not hear another note from the Jonas Brothers. However, in the wee hours of the morning when the only creature stirring is me, I prefer to use in-ear headphones, which shut out everything except the music.

At work, I hardly ever use headphones due to the telephone ringing off the hook, but at lunchtime I sometimes use the in-ear headphones for peace and quiet. I drive to work, so no headphones are needed for the daily commute.

This is a fairly expensive model, but it's worth every cent if you can safely use headphones that cut out most external noise.

Pros:

1. Really nice packaging, easy to open, simple instruction manual
2. Cool, sleek and compact black metal carrying case included, with a cleaning tool and cable clip as accessories.
3. It comes with three different sizes of rubber caps, and as Goldilocks might say, one is for ears that are big, one's for smaller ears, and one will no doubt be just right. Changing caps is simple too.
4. It also includes a pair of memory foam sleeves that fit so snugly in your ears that you may think they belong there.
5. The caps are washable, once you dry them properly before using them again.
6. The sound is marvelous, clear and true, and there's no need to raise the volume to sonic boom levels.
7. The headphones are clearly marked left and right, and are at an angle for easy insertion and a tight seal
8. Drastically cuts down on external noise

Cons:

1. Unless you're using it for an IPod or other portable device, the cord is too short.
2. May feel a bit weird for some people due to the superior noise isolation.
3. You may experience "ewwwwwwwwwww" moments when your friends grab them and try them on. These aren't for sharing.
4. Try saying "in-ear headphones" out loud six times

If you're looking for an excellent pair of (deep breath) in-ear headphones, I think you'll be pleased with this one.

Amanda Richards, July 2, 2008
text_fidelity_b: Philips SHE9850 in-Ear Headphones with Advanced Acoustics (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Everything is as good or better here, except I desperately miss the structured cabling for my network that I installed at the previous house.

I was so relieved when I got to the new place and just set my whole network up in an extra bedroom (until a proper telecomm closet can be brought online) and my Netgear Pro AP is doing a surprisingly great job. No problems keeping VPN connections up and no problems streaming video from my Plex server to the TVs. A lot less reconnect issues than you would have had even a few years ago.

There are plenty of slow spots for long range devices, especially in the basement and back yard. So I figured I'd try this as another interim solution to keep my new wiring project from becoming too pressing. Again, I'm truly surprised how well this works without having created any new issues for me. I had to use the app because my AP doesn't have WPS and I wasn't immediately certain whether this would have an IP address or not. But I got it up and running and just let it alone...surprisingly seamless.

All this WiFi will never be enough to satisfy me for the long term, but having a network that basically works right off the bat with barely any work involved has been a huge relief in getting settled in to the new place.

Oh, and I like that there is a network port on this. Obviously, that isn't a full solution, but taking out any piece of the wireless puzzle is always a step in the right direction.

The presentation is great. The box is very high quality, reminiscent of the recent Samsung Galaxy device boxes. A smooth matte feel with gloss--weirdly pristine. The box slides out of the slipcover and you get the headphones already in the case. What I like is that they're folded, and there's even a little sheet underneath the phones that always reminds you how to put them back in. Also included is a 3.5mm cable in case you don't want to use Bluetooth, a charging cable, and an adapter. The case is nice, but as I keep mine at work I can't testify to its durability. There's a thin mesh net on the backside in case anyone needs to store one or two thin headphone accessory/-ies along. The accent colors are a nice light copper/rose gold color. I love that color; I'm glad it's getting more attention in recent years.

It didn't take long to charge the headphones, so they come with a little bit of juice. As soon as you turn them on, you get a soft beep along with a voice indicating they're turned on. Nice responsive feedback. Once I put them on I could hear the headphones working to drown out the sound; there was a thick veil of soundproofing that was draped over my ears as soon as the earpads touched them.

The first thing I did was listen to podcasts through the Pocket Casts app and .flac music through Poweramp v3. With podcasts, the difference was phenomenal. Listening to "Wait, wait... Don't tell me!" made me feel as though I were in the audience. The music was fantastic...until I tried on my other headphones which I use for music only.
I thought the bass might've been too strong with the Sony headphones, and I was right. After using even "cheaper" headphones like the Audio-Technica M50x, I could tell the Sony had too much bass. I'm not sure if that's partly because of the noise-canceling technology or what, but the bass can be toned down a bit, methinks.

I then proceeded to download the supplementary app to get the fullest suite of attributes the headphones can get. The app works well, and I didn't experience any hiccups while actually using the app. The only hiccup was when I was trying to download the update. It took *forever*. Almost an hour and it was just halfway through. I decided to bring them to work the next day and let the app sit there while updating. Thankfully, it remembers the progress, even though the app kept crashing during the update process.

There are some optimization tweaks in the app, some sound profiles to let you configure the noise cancelation level (yes, level; the noise cancelation is pure software; you can set it to drown out the most noise as possible or have no noise cancellation at all), and even a little snippet of what is currently playing through the headphones. A simple UI with all the features you need.

The first few days I used it I was active, and I kept noticing that my ears sometimes would pop depending on whether I sat down or arose quickly. Another weird thing is that when I take the headphones off, my ears sometimes need a minute or two to adjust. There's so much noise in the world! After taking the headphones off I can hear HVAC activity and my loud work neighbor who's otherwise not that loud.

I had some headphones with some touch controls before and always found them tacky. I used them once when I first got them and never again. But with these headphones, I'm always using the tap gesture to play/pause and the swipe gesture to raise or lower the volume. There are also swipe gestures to skip or go back a track, but since I never do that anyway I never use those gestures. You have to be careful with the tap; when it works, it works. But the whole surface isn't the active portion and you have to hit it right in the center. Sometimes I'm hitting my finger against my ears trying to find the spot and hurting myself in the process. I tested the gesture where you put your entire palm on the cup to turn off the noise canceling feature and let the mic allow incoming conversation, but not after the third try. I could hear the other people just fine, but I found the right hand over my ear felt awkward, and one person didn't realize I could even hear them. Putting your hand over your headphones isn't a gesture people immediately see as you paying attention to them.

The headphones are extremely lightweight and comfortable to use; I left them on for about two hours once before having to take them off. I actually was surprised with how light they were; when I got the Amazon box I didn't believe it was my headphones. It was much lighter than expected.

For my first noise-canceling headphones I'm pleased. The sound balance can be better (less bass), but they make for fantastic headphones to use at work. I wasn't sure what I was expecting with noise-canceling technology. I thought it would drown out all noises, but you still can hear the occasional mutter; it just won't be distinct.

Oh, forgot to mention the battery life. I charged it only once and have been using it for a week, at about an hour or two each day. Still going well. If you press the power button once it will tell you the battery level. AFter the initial update the voice indicator might give the wrong battery level (it did for me), but give it about ten or fifteen minutes to adjust and it will go back to normal.
text_fidelity_b: Sony WH1000XM3 Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Bluetooth Over the Ear Headset – Black (2018 Version)

text_fidelity_a: Google WiFi system, 3-Pack - Router Replacement for Whole Home Coverage (NLS-1304-25),White Easy to setup and works like a charm @ first. Until it didn't. O.k. I must say I know enough about mesh networks to be dangerous but I must say something from the very beginning with the mesh system was strange. Alright it all started back at the beginning of the year where at certain times of night my internet would drag. I said, "NIGHT." Typically in the morning when everyone else is sleep. I am up working. I would notice download speeds of maybe about 25 and uploads at 10. So after a few days of this,  I contacted Xfinity internet support and ask them to run a check on the internet. Right away, the support guy said, "Log into your account and let me show you something."  I said O.k. and right there I am seeing the traffic go thru the roof. The rep said, "Oh yes there is a lot of traffic on for some reason coming from Somalia. I said are you sure. He said Oh yes.  Since I run a business I have backup internet thru another company that I can jump on in case my internet goes down.  So I disconnected my internet and and change the wifi mesh name and password. Later that morning, I noticed that the ssid was still broadcasting my old ssid name so I connected too it and noticed that I still had internet.  REALLY!!!!! I could watch movies and everything. Very strange. So I contacted Google support and was told to reset the mesh back to the original factory systems. Now for the last 4 to 5 months I have to change my ssid every few months and reset everything back to factory settings to keep my internet from dragging. I haven't read anything else about this expect a few bloggers and you-tubers say that they suspect that the mesh network can be hacked.  I must say after a few months of tracking my internet usage online I must say I suspect the same. If you purchase this check your usage regularly.  I have owned this mesh system since 2017 and didn't notice any problems until recently. Trying a new mesh network. It think it is time.

text_fidelity_a:
SABRENT 4TB Rocket NVMe PCIe M.2 2280 Internal SSD High Performance Solid State Drive (SB-ROCKET-4TB) So, I've had this thing for a few months, and it is no longer working. I put my OS (Win10) on it, and everything seemed fine. The NVMe has a heat shield on it that has a fan, so the temps never got as high as some people have reported.

However, the performance of my computer slowly declined until I could no longer rely on the computer to not crash randomly within 30 minutes of starting it. Everything was failing. I could not figure out what the heck was going on. Started troubleshooting everything. Couldn't get through a memtest, so I bought some new ram so I can use my computer while I wait for the G.Skill RMA process. However, even with the new ram, the PC cannot boot with the Sabrent NVMe. Does not proceed further than the loading screen.

Tried booting into safe mode, which failed, as well as resetting the computer through the windows troubleshooting tool. Nothing would go past the loading screen. I've added another photo showing that substantial loss of performance, even while it is not being used by anything else. Keep in mind that although the numbers are mostly higher than the SATA SSD, a loss in performance like this is a tell-tale sign that it is failing. If you notice something similar with your hardware, back up what you want to keep immediately.

Tried booting from my older SSD, and was able to boot just fine. I am still somehow able to access the information on the NVMe when booting from another SSD, but the system is unstable while running on it. I will continue to try to get a replacement or a refund before conceding that I have a $120 tax for trying to save money.

I tried to use the tool to check if there was a firmware update. Doesn't work, as it said cannot find information on the hardware. This is with the latest everything. Seemed odd, so I sent an email to the bug reporting email they provide. Got a response from google saying that email does not exist....

I reached out to Sabrent technical support. No response after a week.

I'm very disappointed. I've gotten other sabrent hardware before and hadn't had problems. Looks like their memory is not their game. Even worse that their customer support is non-existent. Don't expect to get help if you run into the same issue that I got.

text_fidelity_a:
ECLIPSE PHOTO GROUP Front and Rear Professional Lens Protectors As someone who works with cameras for a living, I tend to occasionally misplace/lose my lens caps. Having a one-size-fits-all backup like this claims to be, is therefore intriguing to me.
What I found however, is that this fits alright for smaller sized primes (such as those with a front element of 52mm), but a lot of my zooms or larger primes with bigger front elements are difficult or impossible to fit over. Rear cap was also somewhat of a hit-or-miss; I own E-mount, EOS, Nikon F, Minolta A-mount and Micro4/3 lenses, and none of them are too large in their rear element, but some lenses get wide right after the mount and won't allow a cover like this to squeeze over easily. Some of the smaller primes, especially pancake lenses like the Canon 40mm STM, really can't fit both a front and rear "cap" like this since the entire lens would be engulfed in one end or the other.
On top of all that, even if it DOES fit over your lens, I'm cynical as to how how useful it really is. The purpose of a lens cap is to protect the glass from two things: getting dirty and getting damaged. For starters, the material is soft and won't prevent a hard object collision. I'm not exactly willing to test that theory but considering I can press in and feel the glass through the cover, I'm guessing a hard object in your camera bag could still hit it and crack/shatter/damage it. Perhaps the rubber would soften the blow, but a real lens cap would prevent any blow from happening in the first place!
For dust and debris protection, perhaps it is a little useful, however this sort of material tends to attract a lot of static cling. Just leaving it in my gear bag for a bit, I'm finding dust and hair clinging to it like a balloon. Now, it is possible that means the dust/debris will stick to the cap and not your lens, which is useful, however it doesn't give me a lot of confidence to see stuff stuck to the thing I'm about to use to protect my lens from more of that stuff.

I suppose it's good as a backup in my gearbag in case I lose another lens cap and want something to keep dust off it until I get a replacement, but otherwise I'd strongly recommend getting a proper front and end cap for your lenses.
text_fidelity_b: ECLIPSE PHOTO GROUP Front and Rear Professional Lens Protectors

Seagate 600 SSD 480 GB SATA 6 Gb/s 2.5-Inch 7mm Z-Height Solid State Drive ST480HM000 Though I have a laptop, I decided to use this solid-state drive as a boot drive on my desktop computer. If you are unfamiliar with the difference between a solid-state and a regular hard drive, the solid-state has no moving parts, which makes it silent, fast, reliable, and shock resistant. It has twice the capacity and twice the speed of the solid-state drive I got a couple of years ago for the same price, and blows away a standard drive for speed.

Given the silence and speed, it makes a great boot drive for running Windows, Photoshop, and other programs where speed is a huge advantage. Just to give you an idea, when upgrading from a regular two-year-old hard drive to this solid-state drive, my Windows boot time went from two minutes to about 10 seconds. Seriously, my computer now starts up and is ready to use in like 10 seconds.

What I do is use a solid-state drive as my boot drive and a regular hard drive as a storage drive. Solid-state drives like this are really expensive to purchase if you need any kind of capacity, but a 200 GB drive will certainly hold all of your programs and often used files.

As for this drive specifically, I hooked it up to my desktop and it was immediately recognized by Windows. The drivers installed automatically. In order to make the drive show up as a drive and work in Windows 7, I had to right-click on computer, click manage, double-click storage, double-click disk management, partition it, give it a drive letter, and format it.

As I said, it's a lot faster than the solid-state drive I had from a couple years ago, and there's no problem using it on my desktop machine rather than my laptop.

Antennas Direct ClearStream 1MAX HDTV Antenna UHF VHF, Multi-Directional, 40+ Mile Range, UHD 4K, NEXTGEN TV – w/Adjustable Mounting Hardware (Black) Trying to decide if we were ready to cut the cord, we installed this antenna to see if we could get all the local channels. We got 40 digital channels about 20 miles west of Washington DC and the major networks are crystal clear.

The network towers we use are clustered together about 20 miles away. We have 2 or more topographical obstructions between our house and the towers (no line of sight). The Noise Margin on the networks is 35-40 dB. TVFool.com listed my location as "yellow" (which means use an attic antenna or higher). The cable drop is about 25 feet and I did not use an amplifier.

This antenna is supposed to be omni-directional but we did experience occasional signal drop on the networks with the initial "eyeball" installation (which was off about 15 degrees). Standing directly under the antenna and looking through a compass I had my son walk through the yard until he stepped into the path to the towers. Then I had him stand still, facing the antenna, and rotated it until he told me it was pointed straight over his head. That seemed to fix the signal drops. Given all the factors of our situation, I am probably maxing out the performance of this antenna. If I have any issues I'll just buy the add-on the reflector shield to increase directional performance...but for right now I don't need it.

Installation was easy (I just mounted it to the Direct TV mast). This antenna is small and light which was a big plus when climbing up a 25 foot ladder.

So far so good!
text_fidelity_b: Antennas Direct ClearStream 1MAX HDTV Antenna UHF VHF, Multi-Directional, 40+ Mile Range, UHD 4K, NEXTGEN TV – w/Adjustable Mounting Hardware (Black)

SanDisk Cruzer Fit CZ33 32GB USB 2.0 Low-Profile Flash Drive- SDCZ33-032G-B35 Capacity is more than adequate for my needs, and the price is right. But the real reason why I gave it five stars is this drive is absolutely reliable. I have tried other brands only to experience premature death of the drive, data loss and other frustrations. In fact, one would get so hot in large transfers that it was uncomfortable to touch. This one does not have those flaws.

I use a pair of these. One for backing up my documents on my ThinkPad T61 running Win XP, and the other as a portable music library. For the latter use I've plugged it into my Galaxy Note 3 phone and Samsung tablet via a [[ASIN:B00C7SK2J2 Micro USB OTG Host Cable to USB 2.0 Adapter]], as well as a number of PCs and laptops of fellow musicians.

Just about every operating system, from my Android phone to a friend's Win 8 laptop immediately recognized this as a drive as soon as it was inserted in the USB port.

I did not bother measuring the transfer speed because I mostly use this for streaming music via USB. I have never experienced a freeze or lag in playing, so, again, I am very pleased with it. The final reason why I am happy is the small form factor, which is about the size of a bluetooth dongle.

Bottom line is you can save a few bucks by purchasing a competing brand, but you will get what you pay for in my opinion. I've been using this brand for literally decades and have never had to worry about failure or other issues.

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Basics On-Ear Headphones I use headphones very frequently under a number of different environments including noisy computer labs, airplanes, quiet rooms and more. I am particularly familiar with noise canceling phones but I do have a some non-ANC phones that I use for listening to music in quiet environments. This pair of Amazon Basics headphones is my least expensive pair but it actually compares reasonably well against some more expensive phones.

First, the Basics headphones are very lightweight on-ear phones. They are slightly tight though not so tight to cause discomfort. What they do cause for me is a bit of warmth on the ears, something that I have not experienced very often when using headphones. It’s a minor aggravation, not a show-stopper by any means.

The most important feature of any headphones is the sound profile. I like electronic music which has a wide range of sound frequency - abundant highs, full midrange and quite a bit of bass. When listening to tracks with these phones, the first thing that I could not help but notice is that they overdrive the bass a little much, but this seems to be more the norm with headphones anymore. The highs sound just about right - not exceptionally sharp but not muted either. The midrange, though, is off and reminds me of listening to music in a tunnel. It isn’t terrible, but it’s noticeable. From what I can tell, the bass is so overdriven that it partially flattens the midrange.

I compared these headphones to a pair of Munitio PRO40 phones, a much more expensive set ($350 full retail) of phones that I use for studio work. Yes, the Munitio phones outperformed the Basics phones, but the difference did not match the $300 price difference. Other than the midrange, the Basics phones compared very well on the sound spectrum. That’s more than I could have asked for at $15.

If this was an expensive set of phones I would be very upset. However, this is a VERY inexpensive set and for the price range sounds much better than average.

Construction-wise this set of phones feels well-made. They won’t hold up to abuse, but with proper care they should last a long time. They even come with a cloth carry bag with offers little more than scratch protection but it’s a nice touch.

Considering how inexpensive these headphones are, I am hard-pressed to criticize. In their price range they are well above average in terms of sound and construction. If you are looking for a lightweight and inexpensive set of headphones and you do not need the very best in sound this is an outstanding value.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics On-Ear Headphones
